name: Seneca
quote: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
hook: Most of what you fear will never happen.
script: I am Seneca. Nearly two thousand years ago, I wrote to a friend: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality. Most of what you dread will never happen. Swipe, and I will show you how to stop it.

morning_slides.title: Your mind rehearses disasters that never arrive.
body: Seneca noticed we are rarely crushed by what is actually happening. We are worn down by what we imagine might happen: the bad news, the hard conversation, the worst case.
In the same letter he wrote: “Some things torment us more than they ought; some torment us before they ought; and some torment us when they ought not to torment us at all.”

morning_slides.title: Who was Seneca?
body: A Roman Stoic philosopher, playwright and statesman, and adviser to Emperor Nero.
Late in life he wrote 124 letters to his friend Lucilius: practical advice on living well. Letter 13 is about fear.

morning_slides.title: Next time your mind starts to spiral:
steps: Name the fear in one sentence. Write it down.
Ask Seneca’s question: is this happening now, or only in my head?
If it is real, take one small action. If it is imagined, let it wait until it arrives.

morning_slides.title: What is one fear that never came true?
morning_slides.body: Tell us below. Someone scrolling past needs to read it today.

evening_slides.text: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
Some things torment us more than they ought; some before they ought; and some when they ought not to torment us at all.
Do not be unhappy before the crisis comes.
Most storms pass without ever reaching the shore.
Tonight’s question: what are you worrying about that hasn’t happened yet?

Try this the next time your mind starts to spiral:

2. Ask Seneca’s question: is this happening now, or only in my head?
